verdict: ServiceNow closed 2025 with revenue up 20.5% to $3.57B and $28.2B of future revenue already booked, though $494M of stock pay held GAAP profit to $401M.

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: Companies paying to use the ServiceNow platform — 97% of all revenue; grew 21% YoY (19.5% in constant currency).

segments.name: Professional services
segments.note: Consultants who help customers set the platform up.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the platform to big companies — the largest running cost.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI features.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

otherDetail: Interest income of $105M, less $7M of other expense, net — a net $98M gain outside operations.
oneTimers: Stock-based compensation was $494M in the quarter (including $89M inside cost of revenues) — the main reason non-GAAP net income ($959M) is more than double the GAAP figure ($401M). The cost is real; it is paid in shares instead of cash.
ServiceNow closed its Moveworks acquisition on December 15, 2025; a 5-for-1 stock split also took effect in the quarter (December 17), so per-share figures are split-adjusted.
footerNote: ServiceNow authorized an additional $5B of share repurchases in this release.

takeaways.title: Growth held up
takeaways.text: Total revenue grew 20.5% to $3.57B and subscription revenue 21% — ServiceNow beat its Q4 guidance and finished 2025 with $13.28B of revenue, up 21%.

takeaways.title: Future revenue is booked
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations — revenue customers have signed for but not yet been billed as sales — grew 26.5% to $28.2B, with $12.85B due in the next 12 months.

takeaways.title: Two very different profits
takeaways.text: GAAP EPS was $0.38 against $0.92 non-GAAP: $494M of stock-based compensation is the biggest single difference between the two profit pictures.

follow100Note: Rows are rounded to cents, so the waterfall lands a couple of cents above the $11.24 kept as profit — stock pay, not cash costs, is what holds the GAAP figure down.
